column3: Milady left the room\nin tears.{pause_20_skippable}\nShe hasn't eaten in days.{end_wait}

I pity the warriors
Lord McCoy hired.{page_break}He's blaming them for
the gray sky. Soon he'll
blame us all.{end_wait}
What reward did Lord\nMcCoy give them?\nGold won't keep out ash.{end_wait}
I wish she'd stop\nwailing about the palace.{page_break}We've all lost something.\nMost of us lost more.{end_wait}

They could have lived well
in Bilibin, under Lord
McCoy's roof.{page_break}Why chase danger when
the world is dying
anyway?{end_wait}
I can tell when she's\nupset{em_dash}the whole house\nshakes from her door.{end_wait}

For once, milord stood up
to Lady McCoy.{page_break}He looks bolder. Or
maybe just more
desperate. Hee hee...{end_wait}
Oh!{pause_20_skippable} I thought you\nwere milady.{page_break}You startled me. Everyone\nis on edge lately.{end_wait}
Sometimes a man must\nput his foot down.\nLord McCoy finally did.{end_wait}
The hole in this\nnightgown keeps growing.{page_break}Has somebody been\nwearing it while I sleep?{end_wait}
How reckless, sending\nyoung warriors against\nthe holy tree...{end_wait}
I watched from here.\nAfter all that, you still\nwent to Kolima?{end_now}
I don't know how you broke\nthe curse, but thank\nthe stars you did.{end_wait}

Liar! I saw you walk
through the barricade!{page_break}Then you came back after
the forest turned green.
What did it cost you?{end_wait}
You looked brave walking\ntoward Kolima.\nOr just doomed.{end_wait}
A brave warrior wouldn't\nthink twice about\nbecoming a tree.{end_wait}

The reward you got was
the greatest of treasures.{page_break}Brave people get the
best luck. Or die
first.{end_wait}

That's a fine reward,
but I think you were
just unlucky.{page_break}I don't want you to feel
bad, so here's something
that may help.{end_wait}
She seems okay.\nThank the stars.{end_wait}
The current will drag\nher under if no one\npulls her out!{end_wait}
AHHHH! Please! Anyone!\nHelp me!{end_wait}
Thank you! You pulled me\nout before the river took\nme!{end_wait}
Jill, are these the\nones who saved you?{end_wait}
The river would have\ncarried me away if it\nweren't for you.{end_wait}
I'll never forget what\nyou did for me.\nThank you.{end_wait}
I like this spot by the\nriverbank... The water\nstill sounds peaceful.{end_wait}
I will think of you\nwhenever I taste a\npersimmon.{end_wait}
Whose idea was it to\npick persimmons,\nanyway?{end_wait}
Don't look at me.\nIt wasn't my idea.{end_wait}
These persimmons are\njust like my memories...\nSo{pause_20_skippable} bitter...{end_wait}
We worked so hard...\nIf only we had been\nfaster...{end_wait}
What a cruel world! We\nonly wanted to stand on\neach other's shoulders!{end_wait}
Are you going to cross\nthe bridge?{end_wait}

I thought no one would
ever cross this bridge
again.{page_break}Cross it slowly. It
could be your last time.{end_wait}
You wouldn't understand,\nbut crossing this bridge\nstill feels like a gift.{end_wait}
How did you get here?\nIs the bridge open again?{end_now}

Really?!{pause_20_skippable} Then I can
go home to Kolima?{page_break}I thought I'd never see
home again, with the
cursed forest and all!{end_wait}
Oh... You came through\nthe forest? Then I'll\nstay put.{end_wait}
